g.text: FIGURE 3.3: CONCURRENT MODEL COMPARISON AND SSE STREAMING IN OMNIAI
Two Distinct Real-Time Architectural Capabilities: Asynchronous Concurrency vs. Progressive Token Delivery
SECTION A: CONCURRENT MULTI-MODEL COMPARISON (ASYNC GATHER)
Mechanism: Asynchronous non-blocking concurrency via Python asyncio.gather / Promise.all — Queries two distinct AI architectures simultaneously.
1. User Enters Comparison Prompt
User inputs single prompt & selects Model A (e.g. Gemini) and Model B (e.g. Llama / Qwen)
2. React Frontend Dispatches Comparison Request
HTTP POST /api/compare (Payload: prompt, model_a_id, model_b_id, effort, customKeys)
3. FastAPI Backend Receives & Validates Request
Validates non-empty prompt and distinct model IDs (model_a_id ≠ model_b_id)
4 & 5. Concurrent Asynchronous Task Fork (asyncio.gather)
Spawns independent non-blocking async coroutines: Task A and Task B
Independent monotonic timers initialized via time.perf_counter() for exact latency measurement
BRANCH A (PRIMARY)
BRANCH B (COMPARISON)
EXECUTION PIPELINE A
Provider Adapter A
Formats request envelope & injects API key credentials for Provider A
AI Model A: Google Gemini 3.8 Flash
Direct execution via Google Generative Language REST API
Generated Response A
Full markdown output, code blocks, syntax & explanatory text
Response Time A & Telemetry
Latency: 480 ms | Tokens: 380 | Speed: ~58 tokens/sec
EXECUTION PIPELINE B
Provider Adapter B
Formats request envelope & injects API key credentials for Provider B
AI Model B: Groq Cloud (Llama 3.3 70B / Qwen)
Direct execution via Groq LPU Ultra-Low Latency Inference
Generated Response B
Full markdown output, algorithmic code blocks & complexity analysis
Response Time B & Telemetry
Latency: 220 ms | Tokens: 410 | Speed: ~360 tokens/sec
Comparison Result Processor (Backend Aggregator)
Aggregates model_a and model_b responses, latencies, tokens/sec & records token usage
Side-by-Side Comparison Interface (Frontend CompareView)
Renders dual-column viewport with live speed badges, latency bars & synchronized scrolling
User Evaluates Both Responses (Reasoning, Code & Latency)
SECTION B: SERVER-SENT EVENTS (SSE) STREAMING PIPELINE
Mechanism: Unidirectional persistent HTTP stream (text/event-stream) — Delivers incremental token deltas progressively to the browser without buffering.
1. User Submits a Normal Chat Prompt
Submitted via ChatWindow MessageComposer with model selection & optional document context
2. Backend Forwards Request to Selected AI Provider
POST /v1beta/models/...:streamGenerateContent (Gemini) or /v1/chat/completions with stream=true (Groq)
3. AI Provider Generates Response Tokens Progressively
Hardware inference runs on external LPU / TPU clusters; emits raw chunk deltas immediately
4. Backend Receives Generated Content (Async Stream)
StreamingHandler unpacks chunk frames and strips protocol delimiters with zero intermediate buffering
5. Backend Sends SSE Events to the Frontend

Format: data: {"type": "token", "token": "..."}
(Flushes token envelope immediately)
Headers: Content-Type: text/event-stream; Cache-Control: no-cache; Connection: keep-alive
6. Frontend Progressively Updates Assistant Response
useChat hook appends incoming delta chunks to active message state (accumulatedContent)
7. User Sees the Response Without Waiting for Complete Generation
Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) < 150 ms; seamless typewriter stream effect
User Abort Signal
Generation Cancellation Subsystem
• Client invokes AbortController.abort() on "Stop" button click
• Backend catches ClientDisconnect and terminates upstream provider HTTP request
• Prevents wasted compute tokens and closes SSE stream gracefully
Stream Error
Stream Error & Exception Handling
• Catches HTTP 429 (Rate Limits) or 503 (Upstream Outage)
• Emits structured error event: data: {"type": "error", "message": "..."}
• UI renders non-blocking retry banner without crashing React DOM
Stream Completed & Conversation Persisted
Emits type: "done"; conversation updated in SQLite and local client storage
COMPLETED CONVERSATION TURN
ARCHITECTURAL DISTINCTION SUMMARY FOR UNIVERSITY THESIS:
1. Concurrency (Section A):
Executes two separate AI models in parallel via Python asyncio.gather / Promise.all to produce empirical latency & quality benchmarks.
2. SSE Streaming (Section B):
A progressive delivery mechanism that eliminates waiting time for single-model inference by streaming token deltas over HTTP with cancel/error recovery.
